classification.difficultyReason: Infer missing offsets from parallel and equal sides, use Pythagoras to obtain sloping sides or radii, and combine the correct exterior segments with semicircular or sector arcs.

content.prompt: Find the perimeter of these shapes. Answer to 1 d.p.

spec.description: Trapezium with an outward semicircle on its right, a dashed shared diameter, parallel-arrow marks and a right-angle mark.
spec.mathematics: Parallel edges are 3.5 km and 8.5 km; perpendicular height and semicircle diameter are 7 km. The sloping exterior edge is found from legs 5 km and 7 km.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens appear; the missing sloping length and perimeter are withheld.

answer.worked:
The horizontal difference is $8.5-3.5=5\text{ km}$. Let $s$ be the sloping side.
$$\begin{align*}s&=\sqrt{5^2+7^2}\\s&=\sqrt{74}\text{ km}\\P&=8.5+3.5+\sqrt{74}+\frac12\pi(7)\\P&\approx31.6\text{ km}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Semicircle above an isosceles trapezium, retaining double side ticks, parallel arrows, dashed diameter and altitude, and a right-angle mark.
spec.mathematics: Semicircle diameter is 6 cm; lower base is 10.5 cm; perpendicular height is 3.5 cm. Each equal sloping side has horizontal offset (10.5−6)/2.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens appear; offsets, sloping lengths and perimeter are withheld.

answer.worked:
The equal sloping sides give equal horizontal offsets. Let $d$ be one offset and $s$ one sloping side.
$$\begin{align*}d&=\frac{10.5-6}{2}\\d&=2.25\text{ cm}\\s&=\sqrt{2.25^2+3.5^2}\\P&=10.5+2\sqrt{2.25^2+3.5^2}+\frac12\pi(6)\\P&\approx28.2\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: An upper circular arc over an 8 mm base and equal 3 mm vertical sides. Dashed equal radii meet at the base midpoint; single radius ticks are distinct from double vertical-side ticks.
spec.mathematics: Each radius is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 4 mm and 3 mm. Use the stated 106° central angle for arc length; the source drawing is schematic.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied 106° angle and dimensions remain visible; radius and perimeter are withheld.

answer.worked:
The centre is halfway along the base, so each half is $4\text{ mm}$.
$$\begin{align*}r&=\sqrt{4^2+3^2}\\r&=5\text{ mm}\\P&=8+3+3+\frac{106}{360}\times2\pi(5)\\P&\approx23.3\text{ mm}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Vertical left boundary, 6 mm top edge, an external 8 mm dimension to the centre, dashed radius, top-left right-angle marker and outward circular arc.
spec.mathematics: The dashed radius is the hypotenuse of a triangle with perpendicular legs 6 mm and 8 mm. The lower left boundary is another radius. Use the stated 142° arc angle; the source drawing is schematic.
